name: Books, stationery and school supplies

problems.words: Parents send booklist photos on WhatsApp and we type them up by hand
quick_ideas: Build a master list of each school's class booklists before the rush, because most photos repeat the same lists
Ask parents to name the school and class instead of sending photos, without collecting student names, because one line replaces a whole typed list.

workzap_build.text: parents pick school and class from a WhatsApp link, the bundle is created automatically and they get a pickup slot, with no retyping.

problems.ask_first: Roughly how many schools' lists do you handle each season?
problems.free_stops: how the booklist library and pre-order link are set up is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many parent booklist photos repeat the same school and class this week, so you see where typing time is being wasted most.
Give one person the job of keeping one notebook of repeated school and class lists, so common orders can be filled without retyping each photo.

problems.words: Customers get the wrong edition and come back angry
quick_ideas: Confirm this year's edition with each school once before stocking, because changes otherwise surface only through complaints
Keep old editions on a separate shelf, because mixing them causes most mistakes.

workzap_build.text: a bundle packing list per class with a barcode check that catches the wrong edition before it leaves.

problems.ask_first: How do you find out a school has changed an edition?
problems.free_stops: the edition library and packing check are detailed in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every return for wrong edition this week by title and shelf location, so you spot whether the mix-up starts in stocking or picking.
Make one person check edition and year against the shelf label before handover, so angry returns drop at the counter instead of after collection.

problems.words: Back-to-school week, we can't serve the crowd
quick_ideas: Pre-pack bundles for your biggest schools before the rush, because packing during the queue slows everything
Split collection from new purchases at the counter, because they are different jobs.

workzap_build.text: pre-ordered bundles with pickup slots spread across the week, and a counter list of what's ready.

problems.ask_first: Do most parents buy in the shop or order ahead?
problems.free_stops: slot planning and the pre-order flow go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Watch one busy hour and note where the queue stalls most, so you can ease the exact choke point during back-to-school week.
Give one staff member the job of handing over completed bundles from packing to collection, so counter work keeps moving during the rush.

problems.words: School changed the syllabus and we're stuck with last year's books
quick_ideas: List leftover titles by publisher and whether they're sale-or-return, because some can still go back
Ask schools for next year's lists as early as possible, because late changes cause the overstock.

workzap_build.text: a sale-or-return tracker per publisher with return deadline alerts and a leftover report by title.

problems.ask_first: Can you return unsold books to your suppliers?
problems.free_stops: return deadlines and buying rules are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the shelves and note which old syllabus titles still fill the most space, so you see which leftovers are tying up your season most.
Give one person the job of keeping all old syllabus books in one marked area, so current season stock stays easy to pick and explain.

problems.words: Popular books on the list run out in the first week
quick_ideas: Compare last season's sales with what you ordered for your top titles, because it shows where you under-bought
Order your biggest titles earliest, because publishers deliver late in the rush.

workzap_build.text: demand per title from last year's sales and current pre-orders, with low-stock alerts during the season.

problems.ask_first: How do you decide quantities today?
problems.free_stops: the forecasting method is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Write down each time a listed book is asked for but unavailable this week, so next buying reflects real missed demand.
Give one staff member the job of updating one running shortage list for fast-moving titles, so reordering starts from today's gaps not guesswork.

problems.words: Schools take supplies on credit and pay months later
quick_ideas: Total what each school or office owes and for how long, because it shows who to chase first
Match delivery notes to invoices once, because missing paperwork delays payment.

workzap_build.text: institutional accounts with orders, delivery notes, invoices, ageing and automatic reminders.

problems.ask_first: How many schools or offices buy on credit?
problems.free_stops: account setup and reminder timing go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Count how many school deliveries still lack matching paperwork in your files, so you see what is slowing payment before chasing balances.
Give one person the job of keeping credit deliveries and invoice copies in one folder, so payment follow-up starts with complete papers.

problems.words: Office customers send orders on WhatsApp and they get missed
quick_ideas: Count last week's WhatsApp orders and how many were delivered complete, because it shows the size of the leak
Make one person own office orders, because shared phones lose messages.

workzap_build.text: WhatsApp order intake for offices with confirmation and status, so nothing is missed.

problems.ask_first: How many office customers order regularly?
problems.free_stops: the intake flow is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Note every office order that arrived but was not packed the same day this week, so the leak shows in missed work not impressions.
Give one person the job of writing every office order into one notebook as it arrives, so packing starts from one complete list.

problems.words: Thousands of small stationery items, no idea what's in stock
quick_ideas: Count your top-selling stationery once, because a short list covers most sales
Set a minimum for each of those, because it tells staff when to reorder.

workzap_build.text: stationery stock by SKU with reorder alerts on phone.

problems.ask_first: How do you check stock before reordering now?
problems.free_stops: reorder levels are worked out in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Walk the stationery shelves and note which small items customers ask for most but staff must hunt for, so your blind spots stand out quickly.
Give one staff member the job of keeping one list of fast-moving stationery counts at closing, so replenishing starts from a known short list.

quick_ideas: Note the machine counter at open and close for one week, because it shows what should be in the till
Keep photocopy cash separate, because mixing it hides gaps.

workzap_build.text: a daily photocopy and printing log reconciled with cash automatically.

problems.free_stops: the reconciliation steps go in the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Compare photocopy jobs done with cash handed over at each shift end this week, so you see when the mismatch actually starts.
Give one person the job of counting photocopy cash at every handover in one notebook, so shortages are tied to a specific shift.

problems.words: I don't know how this year's school season compared to last year
quick_ideas: Write down this season's totals by school and title while they're fresh, because memory fades fast
Note what ran out and what was left, because that's next year's buying plan.

workzap_build.text: a season review comparing titles, schools and margins year on year.

problems.ask_first: Where are your season sales recorded today?
problems.free_stops: the review structure is kept for the solution document.

extra_ideas.text: Pull out last year's and this year's school season notebooks and compare which schools, titles, and weeks drove sales, so buying starts earlier where demand really moved.
Give one staff member the job of keeping one season notebook for stockouts, leftovers, and busy school requests, so next year's comparison is ready without chasing scraps.

never_say: Help with photocopied, scanned or pirated books for sale, or printing unlicensed copies.
Advice on copyright or licensing law; say "check with a lawyer".
Anything that needs students' or parents' names, classes or contacts.
Help with kickbacks to schools or tender manipulation.
Advice on school or government contract compliance.

sample_reply.person: Every April parents send booklist pictures on WhatsApp and my staff type everything out. Is there a better way?
sample_reply.pi:
Yes, this can be fixed, and the first steps are simple.
First, build a master list of each school's class booklists before the rush, because most photos repeat the same lists.
Second, ask parents for just the school and class, which replaces a whole typed list.
Workzap could build this for you: parents choose school and class from a link, the bundle is created and they get a pickup slot.

Would you like me to arrange a solution document and quote for you? You're welcome to say no.
